rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Cold-read of new chunk 7 ("Marketplace governance"): 'plugin distribution over plain `claude mcp add`' (line 110) and 'plain Path 1 or Path 2' (line 110) reuse terms named in chunk 1 (line 11-13: item 1 = Claude.ai inheritance / Path 1, item 2 = `claude mcp add` / Path 2) — resolves under sequential-deck-read carve-out, not a violation. 'Pairs with `managed-mcp.json` as the second half of tenant-side plugin policy' (line 108) is self-contained within the sentence (first half = managed-settings.json named same sentence). Harm check: a reader who has read chunks 1-6 in order can resolve every pronoun/named term in chunk 7 without reaching outside the file. Whole-file scan found no 'never named' or 'vague with full history' cases in the other 8 chunks either (e.g. chunk 4 line 77 'the three trackers' resolves to GitHub/Jira/Linear headers already read). Near-miss checked and cleared: line 5 'see the maintainer `Source verification` block' points at content past the `<!-- maintainer -->` cut (never rendered to students) — stays PASS because it's citation-transparency framing an auditor reads, not a claim the student must resolve to use the page; the page functions without following it.

No callback to another curriculum file found anywhere in the body. Closest candidate, line 15: 'Per-tracker install commands come next... under *Plugins and marketplaces* on this page' — names the target section by its actual title (passes §2's 'name it' bar) rather than locating it positionally.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal demo mechanic in this file; it is a flat install/lookup reference.

Every chunk carries a self-sufficient claim, including the two newest ones: chunk 6 (lines 89-103) defines plugin/marketplace and gives the install commands; chunk 7 (lines 104-113) states the official-vs-team distinction, enterprise pre-registration, and the plugin-vs-plain-install decision rule — neither is a wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Chunk 7 header 'Marketplace governance: official vs team, and when to reach for plugin distribution' (line 104) is answered by its own body: official-vs-team (line 106), enterprise pre-registration (line 108), and the decision rule (line 110) — the header is a true summary, not a promise the chunk doesn't keep. Chunk 6 header similarly matches its content (plugin/marketplace definitions + install commands).

Checked all sub-items across all 9 chunks: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlatives (no 'one of the most useful' phrasing anywhere, incl. new chunk 7); no number+retraction pattern; no abstraction-noun stacks; no verb triplets with an empty leg. Grep for banned shapes returned nothing in the body region.

rules_evaluated.evidence: No repo/maintainer vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun) anywhere in the body, including the new chunk 6/7 text. 'scope' appears repeatedly (lines 32, 60, 93, 106, 108) but as ordinary engineering/product usage ('product scopes', 'project scope', 'own scope in the precedence hierarchy') that an engineer reads without decoding — not repo dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-derived independently (prior finding was actioned only one line deep). This file is a declared 'Flat lookup' (line 1), which invokes §9's lookup-surface waiver (per-slide bold-count budget off) — but the waiver explicitly leaves the ≲5-word handle cap in force ('bold the mode word alone... leave the title plain'), and that cap is broken repeatedly, in both pre-existing and newly-split chunks: chunk 3 line 50 '**CLI install (when you want project scope or a different Claude.ai account):**' = 12 words; chunk 7 line 110 '**When to reach for plugin distribution over plain `claude mcp add`.**' = 11 words; chunk 4 line 79 '**Fallbacks when a tenant blocks the first-party server:**' = 9 words; chunk 2 line 32 '**When to add the official GitHub MCP server instead.**' = 9 words; chunk 6 line 95 '**Add a marketplace, then install a plugin:**' = 7 words; chunk 6 line 93 '**How MCPs ride inside plugins.**' = 6 words. Chunk 2 additionally breaks the non-menu narrative budget itself (not just the cap): line 23 '**Default for AE101: `gh` CLI (Path 3).**' and line 32 both bold full-sentence leads on one slide that is a stance/explainer, not a scanned menu — two bolds where the non-waived budget allows one, and both are whole sentences rather than sub-span handles. Chunk 3 line 60 '**individual engineers don't need per-install admin approval**' is bold placed mid-paragraph on ordinary narrative prose, which §9 bans outright regardless of length ('Narrative... mechanism prose = no bold'). Harm check: these are full clauses standing in for handles, so a reader scanning bold-as-navigation lands on a sentence instead of a term — the finding-aid function the waiver exists to protect is undercut by its own overuse.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Trim each flagged bold to its actual handle (the noun/mode word), e.g. line 110 → bold just 'plugin distribution' or drop the bold and let the heading carry it; unbold the narrative aside at line 60 entirely.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule 15's grammar split is stated only for exercise headings (imperative/phase label) vs lecture headings (claims) — this file is a reference page, a third file type the rule doesn't address. Checked anyway for fit: all headings here, including the new 'Marketplace governance: official vs team, and when to reach for plugin distribution' (line 104), are noun-phrase topic labels — consistent with the lookup-surface register the compendium describes elsewhere (§9), not a mismatch against either the exercise or lecture grammar this rule actually governs.
